newsitem.title: USA: NY MTA plans to buy more subway cars than expected.
newsitem.headline: NY MTA plans to buy more subway cars than expected.

text.p: Metropolitan Transportation Authority of New York said it expects to be able to buy 1,080 new subway cars -- 340 more than first anticipated -- because it drove hard bargains.

Saying the agreements, which MTA's board will consider Wednesday, were the result of round-the-clock negotiations, the Authority said, "This process generated a highly competitive atmosphere, in which the MTA secured extremely advantageous pricing." The prepared remarks were released late Tuesday.

The New York Times in its Wednesday edition said that the Authority was expected to spend $1.4 billion to buy the new cars, which will replace most of the fleet's 1,400 "corroding, barn-red" cars built after 1959. The paper added the new cars will mainly run on the Number 2, 4 and 7 lines. A spokesman for the Authority was not immediately available to comment.
The purchases will be split between two manufacturers, with the Authority buying 680 from Bombardier's Plattsburgh facility, and 400 from Kawasaki Rail Car Inc in Yonkers, the Authority said.

Bombardier, in prepared remarks, said the work will generate a total of 1,300 jobs at its Plattsburgh and Auburn plants, requiring 450 new jobs. The firm, which plans to spend over $18 million on capital projects at its Plattsburgh plant and $2.5 million at Auburn to fulfill the Authority's order, set the total value of its new contract at $1.15 billion. The $921 million contract includes an option for up to 200 extra cars, to be exercised by January 2000, it explained.
